creator_or_organization: EuropIA Institute, in partnership with the City of Cannes (under Mayor David Lisnard), the Palais des Festivals et des Congres, and the Alpes-Maritimes Department. Produced and organized by RX France (formerly Reed Exhibitions France).
language: Multilingual (conferences primarily in English; some demo sessions and SME-focused workshops in French; website available in both English and French)
content_focus: Business-oriented AI conference covering the full spectrum of AI's impact on business and society. The 2026 edition (5th) focuses on 4 key sectors: (1) Banking & Finance — AI for risk assessment, fraud detection, customer experience, regulatory compliance; (2) Healthcare — AI-driven diagnostics, treatment discovery, personalized care (includes an AI & Healthcare Call for Projects with EUR 30,000-60,000 funding); (3) Manufacturing — process optimization, predictive maintenance, quality assurance; (4) Retail — personalization, supply chain, customer experience. Cross-cutting themes include AI governance and regulation (EU AI Act), ethical and sustainable AI, sovereign European AI solutions, next-generation technologies, and startup innovation. Program format includes: 250+ conference sessions, 45 workshops, 50 startup pitches, 20 immersive experiences, demo zones, and networking platforms. Speakers span industry (Meta FAIR, Google, AWS, IBM, HP, SAP, eBay, Alstom, Accenture, DXC Technology, JPMorgan Chase), government (French Minister Delegate for AI Clara Chappaz, Luxembourg Minister of Finance Gilles Roth), and international organizations (OECD Director Jerry Sheehan).
target_audience: Business leaders, enterprise decision-makers, AI entrepreneurs, startup founders, investors, corporate innovation teams, policymakers, and the general public (dedicated public day). Non-technical framing makes it accessible to executives and business professionals, not just engineers.
publication_frequency: Event-based (annual conference, held each February in Cannes since 2022). The 2026 edition is the 5th, scheduled February 12-13, 2026.
format_and_length: 2-day in-person conference at the Palais des Festivals in Cannes (8:30 AM to 6:30 PM). Includes keynote speeches, panel discussions, 45 workshops, 50 startup pitches, 20 immersive experiences, 250+ sessions total, and an exhibition hall with 220+ exhibitors. Previous editions included a third public day with interactive labs and accessible talks.
accessibility_for_non_engineers: High — WAICF is explicitly positioned as an AI event for 'Business & Society,' not a technical research conference. Content is framed around business impact, industry use cases, and societal implications rather than algorithms or code. Workshops and demo sessions allow hands-on discovery. The exhibition floor showcases real products and solutions. Panel discussions feature executives and policymakers alongside technologists. The free Discovery Pass lowers the barrier to entry. Some sessions are specifically designed for SMEs and non-technical audiences. The public day (in past editions) was dedicated to making AI accessible to the general audience.
signal_to_noise_ratio: High — Curated by RX France (a major global events company) with 320+ vetted international speakers and 220+ exhibitors. Focus on concrete business applications and real-world case studies rather than hype. Startup pitches are selected through a competitive process (WAICF Awards via Agorize platform). The 4-sector focus (banking, healthcare, manufacturing, retail) ensures depth over breadth.
unique_value_proposition: The largest European AI conference specifically positioned at the intersection of business and society, hosted in the iconic Palais des Festivals in Cannes. Unique combination of: (1) European-first perspective on AI governance and sovereignty; (2) High-level institutional speakers (French ministers, OECD, EU officials) alongside industry leaders; (3) Startup ecosystem visibility with 50 startup pitches and WAICF Awards competition; (4) French/European regulatory context (EU AI Act, GDPR) baked into discussions; (5) Accessible to non-technical audiences with free Discovery Pass and public programming; (6) Strong networking infrastructure with 600+ facilitated business meetings. Unlike NeurIPS or ICML (research-focused) or CES (consumer tech), WAICF bridges AI technology with business strategy and policy in a European context.
free_or_paid: Freemium — Discovery Pass is free (access to exhibition area, demo sessions, and startup conferences). Full Pass costs EUR 1,090 (access to all conference sessions plus professional networking platforms). Payment by credit card or bank transfer.
source_reliability: High — Organized by RX France (part of RELX Group, a FTSE 100 company), one of the world's largest event organizers. Backed by the City of Cannes and the EuropIA Institute (a recognized European AI policy organization). Speakers include verified leaders from major corporations, government officials, and international organizations. The Palais des Festivals venue (home of the Cannes Film Festival) provides institutional credibility. Now in its 5th edition, the event has established a track record with consistent growth (from first edition in April 2022 to 10,000-16,000 attendees by 2024-2025).
relevance_for_entrepreneurs: Very high relevance for AI entrepreneurs, especially those targeting European markets. Provides: (1) Direct exposure to enterprise buyers — 10,000+ decision-makers from banking, healthcare, manufacturing, and retail; (2) Startup showcase — 50 startup pitches and WAICF Awards offer visibility and potential funding; (3) Regulatory intelligence — firsthand access to policymakers shaping EU AI Act implementation, critical for compliance planning; (4) Business meeting facilitation — 600+ structured networking opportunities; (5) European market positioning — understand what European enterprises actually need vs. US-centric conferences; (6) Investment landscape — connect with European investors and corporate innovation teams; (7) Competitive intelligence — see what 220+ exhibitors are building and selling in your space.
actionable_insight_level: High — Conference content is designed around real business applications and case studies, not abstract research. Startup pitches demonstrate market-ready solutions. Workshops provide hands-on methodology. Networking platforms facilitate concrete business conversations. The EU governance track provides directly actionable regulatory compliance guidance.
session_mapping: S1 (Fundamentals — AI landscape overview and key actors), S4 (Business Models — industry case studies, startup pitches, business strategy), S5 (Ethics/Governance — EU AI Act, responsible AI, European sovereignty)
ecosystem_position: Primary source / Major industry event — WAICF is the largest European AI conference focused on the business-society intersection, positioned as the '#1 AI Event for Business & Society.' It serves as a primary networking and deal-making platform rather than a content aggregator. Within the European AI conference landscape, it occupies a distinct niche between pure research conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, AAAI) and broad tech expos (VivaTech, Web Summit). It is a key venue where European AI policy (EU AI Act, GDPR) meets business implementation, and where the French/European AI ecosystem (Mistral AI, LightOn, etc.) showcases to global enterprise buyers. Partners include 3IA Cote d'Azur (Interdisciplinary Institute for Artificial Intelligence), hub.brussels, InnovationQuarter, and numerous European AI clusters.
recommendation_tier: Nice-to-Have (attend if possible when in Europe in February; otherwise follow highlights and speaker content online. The free Discovery Pass makes physical attendance very accessible for students.)
